summary.title: Part 2 - Simple Communication
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a basic WebSocket echo server in Go using gorilla/websocket and connect a ReactJS frontend to it for two-way messaging.
keywords: send websocket message from react button
takeaways: Install github.com/gorilla/websocket and use its Upgrader to convert an HTTP endpoint into a WebSocket endpoint.
Read messages in a loop with conn.ReadMessage() and echo them back with conn.WriteMessage().
Use the browser WebSocket API (onopen, onmessage, onclose, onerror, send) to connect a React app to the Go server.
WebSockets avoid repeated polling and TCP handshakes, but stateful connections complicate scaling across multiple instances.
summary.summary: This tutorial is part 2 of a series building a chat app with a Go backend and ReactJS frontend. It starts with a simple net/http server, then explains the WebSocket protocol trade-offs, including scaling concerns for stateful connections. It adds a /ws endpoint using gorilla/websocket that echoes messages back, and a JavaScript api module plus a React button that sends a message over the socket. The page ends with a question about the console output from clicking the button.
